bifrost: springboard/src/shell/widgets/mod.rs, springboard/src/shell/today.rs, springboard/src/shell/homeconf.rs, springboard/src/shell/widgetgallery.rs, springboard/src/shell/homeedit.rs, springboard/src/shell/control_center.rs, springboard/sdk/src/widgets.rs (drawing kit, not WidgetKit)
summary: BifrOSt has shell-owned home-screen and Today widgets (a fixed set of nine kinds, with small and medium sizes, a Smart Stack and an Add Widget gallery) and Control Center toggles, all drawn by the shell. There is no app-facing WidgetKit equivalent: apps cannot ship a widget extension, a timeline provider, a Live Activity, an app-provided control, or a widget intent. The SDK widgets module is a drawing kit for app windows, not a widget API.

features.feature: Widget extension and widget configuration (Widget, WidgetBundle, StaticConfiguration)
features.bifrost: springboard/ui/src/widget_kind.rs; springboard/src/shell/services/widgets_timeline.rs (register, sync_manifests); springboard/sdk/src/widgets_timeline.rs (Kind, register); springboard/src/shell/apphost.rs (Manifest::widgets); springboard/ui/src/widget_kind.rs (parse_manifest)
features.note: The widget kind registry (identifiers, sizes, bundles, lookups by size) is tested headless in springboard/ui/tests/parity_sdk-tests-10-w7.rs. Not wired into apps or the shell, and not yet tested on the VM or Midget. Widgets are compiled into the shell. No app can register a widget kind, and there is no bundle or extension process. Built 2026-10-19: an app registers the widget kinds it offers, either with the widgets_timeline service call register (SDK Kind and register: id, name, description, sizes) or as [[widget]] tables in manifest.toml (id, name, description, families, configurable), which the shell reads for every installed app and registers on its tick. A registered kind is in the Edit Widgets gallery before its first timeline, keeps the person's choices (placed, size, options) across re-registration and reloads, and moves to its smallest size when a new registration drops the size it had. Tests: ui widget_kind::tests (manifest_tables_become_kinds_*, a_bad_table_is_dropped_*), services widgets_timeline::tests (a_registered_kind_is_in_the_gallery_*, a_kind_takes_only_the_sizes_it_registered_*, registering_checks_the_kinds, a_registered_kind_takes_options_*), sdk widgets_timeline::tests (a_register_call_names_each_kind_*). Still no separate extension process or widget bundle type for apps: the app itself answers reload events. Midget check: click the clock in the menu bar, Edit Widgets: a widget kind an app declares with [[widget]] in its manifest.toml (for example id = "next-event", name = "Next Event", families = ["small", "medium", "large"]) is listed with its name and description and one chip per declared size, before the app has run.

features.feature: Widget families and sizes (systemSmall, systemMedium, systemLarge)

features.bifrost: springboard/src/shell/homeconf.rs (Size, cells); springboard/src/shell/widgets/mod.rs (SMALL_PT 155, MEDIUM_PT 329, Kind::size); tests: springboard/tests/parity_sdk-tests-01b.rs; springboard/src/shell/services/widgets_timeline.rs (Widget::family, set_family); springboard/ui/src/widget_column.rs (flow); springboard/src/shell/notify/center.rs (center_widget_rects, size chips)
features.note: Small and medium families only, in points and grid cells (headless_widget_families_* in springboard/tests/parity_sdk-tests-01b.rs). The Large flag in the timeline store makes a row taller in Notification Centre; it is not a systemLarge family. Apps cannot choose a family. Built 2026-10-19: Small, Medium and Large are real families end to end. A kind supports the sizes it registered (kinds that were only reloaded keep Small and Large); Edit Widgets shows one chip per supported size (Small, Medium, Large) and set_family refuses a size the kind does not support; the Notification Centre column draws a row as tall as its family (58, 77 or 96 pt) and stacks the rows with widget_column::flow, which keeps the leading rows that end above the dock. The app sees the size in the widgets call (family, families) and the visibility event keeps reporting large. Tests: widget_column::tests (flowed_rows_*, the_first_row_that_crosses_the_bottom_*), widgets_timeline::tests (a_registered_kind_is_in_the_gallery_*, a_kind_takes_only_the_sizes_it_registered_*). The row layout is a stack of text lines; an app does not yet get a per-family layout. Midget check: click the clock in the menu bar, Edit Widgets: a widget registered with three sizes shows Small, Medium and Large chips; choose Medium, tap Done and the widget row is taller than Small and shorter than Large.

features.feature: Dynamic dates and clock content in widgets
features.apple: Displaying dynamic dates in widgets, Text date styles
features.bifrost: springboard/ui/src/widget_date.rs (text, next_change); springboard/ui/tests/parity_sdk-tests-11.rs; springboard/src/shell/services/widgets_timeline.rs (Clock, Text::display, next_text_change, next_refresh); springboard/sdk/src/widgets_timeline.rs (ClockStyle, Rich::with_clock); springboard/ui/src/widget_date.rs (Style::from_key); springboard/src/shell/notify/center.rs (refresh_due in center_tick)
features.note: Relative and timer wording and the next change instant are tested headless in widget_date::tests and parity_sdk-tests-11.rs. Gap: the model is not wired into apps or the shell, so widgets show no date-styled text yet, and it is untested on Midget. Built 2026-10-19: an entry can carry a clock (style relative or timer, target date). The shell writes the text at draw time (the entry's text with {} replaced, or followed by the wording; a blank text shows the clock alone) so it keeps counting while the app does not run, the current call returns the same wording, and the open column is redrawn when the wording next changes (next_change: each second for a timer or a distance under a minute, then per minute, hour and day). Tests: widget_date::tests (an_app_names_a_style_by_its_key), widgets_timeline::tests (live_date_text_keeps_counting_while_the_app_is_away, a_clock_follows_the_text_or_stands_alone_*, a_bad_clock_is_refused). No date interval, offset or time-zone variants. Midget check: click the clock in the menu bar: a widget whose entry has a relative clock reads, for example, "starts in 4 minutes" and the minutes drop while the column stays open.

features.feature: Interactivity in widgets (Button, Toggle, AppIntent in widget)
features.apple: Button, Toggle, Adding interactivity to widgets and Live Activities
features.bifrost: springboard/ui/src/widget_action.rs (hit_test, Toggle); springboard/ui/src/widget_link.rs (Link); springboard/src/shell/services/widgets_timeline.rs (tap_action, settle_action, Text::buttons); springboard/sdk/src/widgets_timeline.rs (Button, Rich::with_button); springboard/ui/src/widget_action.rs (ButtonSpec, ToggleSet); springboard/src/shell/notify/center.rs (DeskHit::Action, run_widget_action)
features.note: Topmost-region hit testing, link parsing and the toggle that shows a tap and settles on the app's answer are tested headless in springboard/ui/tests/parity_sdk-tests-12.rs; no widget action invokes an app intent, and the shell's tiles only open the shell's own apps. Built 2026-10-19: a widget entry carries up to three buttons or toggles (SDK Button, reload_rich; service reload entries actions). A tap in the Notification Centre column runs the app intent the button names with its string parameters over the app's control socket on a worker thread (the app must be running); a toggle also passes its new state as the parameter on, shows the new state at once, is drawn lighter while it waits and goes back when the intent fails or the app cannot be reached; a second tap while it waits is refused, and a reload brings the app's own state. Ids are checked so no unsafe intent id reaches a request line. Tests: widget_action::tests (a_toggle_sends_its_new_state_*, a_tapped_toggle_shows_the_new_state_*, unsafe_ids_*, an_entry_takes_a_few_buttons_*), widgets_timeline::tests (an_entry_offers_buttons_and_toggles_*, a_tapped_toggle_shows_the_new_state_until_the_app_answers_*, a_widget_action_is_checked_on_reload), sdk widgets_timeline::tests (a_rich_reload_adds_the_clock_buttons_and_link_*). Not started when the app is not running (Apple runs the intent in a widget extension process); no confirmation or authentication step. Midget check: click the clock in the menu bar: the widget row of an app that sends reload_rich with a Button shows a capsule at the right end of the row; click it with the app running and the app's intent runs (for a toggle, the capsule turns blue at once and stays blue while the app answers ok).

gaps: No separate widget extension process: apps register kinds (register or [[widget]] tables) and answer reload events themselves; there is no WidgetBundle or declarative configuration type for apps (widget_kind::WidgetBundle exists as a model only).
Widget buttons run over the app's control socket, so the app must be running; there is no start-on-demand extension (Button, Toggle and AppIntent inside a widget extension).
Timeline API for apps exists (reload, reload_rich, register) but there is no WidgetCenter.reloadAllTimelines call from an app into the shell; shell tiles refresh themselves only.
No Live Activity API (ActivityKit, ActivityConfiguration, DynamicIsland); the lock screen shows shell now-playing only.

No on-screen Control Center panel for app controls yet (ControlWidgetButton, ControlWidgetToggle, ControlValueProvider): manifest [[control]] tables are parsed and registered, but the panel and its Edit Controls gallery do not show them.
No widget container background for the accented look; the accented and vibrant modes exist only as a model (springboard/ui/src/widget_render.rs).
Widget accessibility descriptions are a model only (springboard/ui/src/widget_ax.rs); shell tiles are pixel images.
No relevance input for Smart Stacks; the shell stack is a manual swipe list.
Widget location and network grants are a model only (springboard/ui/src/widget_access.rs); nothing enforces them.
